To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
poly[aniline(50 mol %)-co-5-SO(3)H-2-anisidene(50 mol %)] nanograins exhibit ultrastrong sorption and highly efficient recovery for silver ions as silver crystals.
poly[aniline(50%)-co-5-SO(2)-2-AN(50%)] nanograins exhibit ultrastrong adsorption, highly efficient recovery, and excellent separation capability of silver ions.
the AN/SA (1:1) copolymer nanoparticles exhibit ultrastrong adsorption of Ag(I) as silver nanocrystal precipitates, and thus can be used to recover and purify silver from wastewaters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and application of novel nanosorbent materials for the recovery and separation of silver nanocrystals.
the development of novel functionalized nanomaterials and their application to environmental protection and resource recovery.

the synthesis of a novel polymeric nanosorbent, the study of its sorption and separation mechanisms, the investigation of its adsorption kinetics and isotherm, and the development of a new method for recovery of silver nanocrystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the poly(aniline-co-sulfo-5-anisidine) copolymers have great application potential not only in wastewater treatment, but also in resource reuse, functional hybrid nanocomposite materials, and noble metals industry.
poly(AN-co-SA) nanograins with a rough and porous structure can be used to recover and purify silver ions from industrial wastewaters and to produce silver nanocrystals.
the AN/SA copolymer nanosorbents have been successfully developed for the first time to recover and separate silver nanocrystals by redox sorption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
poly(AN-co-SA) nanograins with a high AN/SA ratio exhibit the strongest Ag(I) sorptivity and can recover silver nanocrystals with the highest purity.

the AN/SA copolymer nanoparticles are a new type of nanosorbent with high sorption capacity, high selectivity, high efficiency, and good stability, and they can be used for highly efficient recovery of Ag(I) ions from practical Ag(I)-bearing wastewater.

the copolymer nanosorbents with a large number of functional groups on their porous surface can be used as an effective and convenient method for the separation and reuse of noble metals from wastewaters containing coexisting ions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
poly(aniline-co-sulfonated aniline)s are promising nanosorbents for recovery of precious metals from wastewaters.
the AN/SA copolymers are promising materials for the recovery of silver from wastewaters.
the AN/SA (AN/SA = 50/50) nanograins exhibit much stronger adsorption and highly effective recovery of silver ions, and thus have great application potential.
